$comment: Deterministic rule catalogue for un-editorial-check. The editorial set (profile: null) is the default; every other set runs only through an explicit audit profile. Validated by lib/config.mjs and asserted against lib/rules.mjs and lib/audits.mjs by the test suite.

rules.guardNotes: Allowlisted terms, quoted titles, URLs, code and comments are outside the extracted copy span and cannot fire.
rules.summary: American spelling used in prose where the profile prescribes the British form.

rules.guardNotes: Emitted per copy block, independently of UE-SP001, so mixed register is visible even when one variant is allowlisted.
rules.summary: British and American variants of the same word used in one passage.

rules.guardNotes: Silent unless spellingReview is true; matching is case-insensitive; size and prize forms are not -ise candidates and are skipped; some -ize spellings are standard (Oxford) and are never claimed as errors.
rules.summary: -ize form that may require an -ise spelling under the named dictionary.

rules.guardNotes: Downgraded to warning with heuristic confidence inside a defining context, where naming the unapproved term may be intentional.
rules.summary: Unapproved indicator or programme term from the organisation profile.

rules.guardNotes: Phrase-aware match on the exact configured term; allowlist entries are checked first.
rules.summary: Unapproved gender, age or population phrasing from the organisation profile.

rules.guardNotes: Skipped in compact surfaces: chart labels, axes, legends, tooltips, stat tiles, <title> and meta description.
rules.summary: Percentage written with the % symbol in running prose instead of per cent.

rules.guardNotes: The suggestion accounts for a preceding the; U.S.A., US dollar and cent amounts and US$ currency figures are excluded.
rules.summary: Bare US used as a country name in prose.

rules.guardNotes: Slash-delimited dates only; ISO machine dates inside URLs and code are outside the copy span.
rules.summary: Numeric d/m/y date instead of the day-month-year written form.

rules.guardNotes: Skipped in compact surfaces; already-en-dashed ranges and version numbers never match.
rules.summary: Numeric range joined with a hyphen instead of an en dash.

rules.guardNotes: Phrase-aware; approved and allowlisted phrases are exempt, and quoted titles are outside the span.
rules.summary: Promotional or non-neutral register term in prose.

rules.guardNotes: The CLI cannot prove or disprove a ranking claim; it routes the claim to review rather than asserting a defect.
rules.summary: Superlative or ranking claim that needs a source or neutral wording.

rules.guardNotes: Clause-level: one hedged sentence does not hedge the next. Figures without a unit word are not prose figures.
rules.summary: Figure stated without a hedge or source in the same sentence.

rules.guardNotes: Sentence-initial question openers ending in a question mark only; a genuine information question can match the same openers, so the sentence is routed to review as a heuristic and never declared a defect.
rules.summary: Rhetorical question used for effect where UN copy states the finding directly.

rules.guardNotes: Comparison operators and shouting markers preceded by =, !, < or > are excluded.
rules.summary: Exclamation mark in formal copy.

rules.guardNotes: A qualifier in the count's own sentence (reported, estimated, total, as of, more than) satisfies the rule; a qualifier in the next sentence does not.
rules.summary: Count that does not say what was counted or whether it is reported, estimated or total.

rules.guardNotes: Requires both multiple years and an explicit comparison phrase; a single year in prose never fires.
rules.summary: Comparison that may be aligning different reference periods.

rules.guardNotes: Bare status assertions only: claims attributed to a reporting party, quoted copy, comments and URLs never reach the rule. Detection is symmetric — every claimant in an entry fires on the same pattern — and each knowledge-base entry cites its source.
rules.summary: Contested sovereignty or territorial-status claim about a listed region stated as fact instead of attributed or phrased in neutral United Nations terminology.

rules.guardNotes: Length measured after entity decoding and whitespace normalisation; never affects the exit code.
rules.summary: Page title missing, empty or longer than the recommended maximum.

rules.guardNotes: Length measured after entity decoding; never affects the exit code.
rules.summary: Meta description missing, empty or longer than the recommended maximum.

rules.guardNotes: Validates declaration syntax and, when configured, the origin; it does not fetch the URL or prove path self-reference.
rules.summary: Canonical link missing, relative, or pointing at a different origin.

rules.guardNotes: Counts literal h1 openings outside comments and scripts is not attempted; it is an audit, not editorial copy.
rules.summary: Page does not have exactly one first-level heading.

rules.guardNotes: Informational only; social cards are a publishing concern, not an editorial one.
rules.summary: Open Graph or Twitter card metadata missing.

rules.guardNotes: Attribute-presence check only; it cannot judge whether the accessible name is a good one.
rules.summary: Image, canvas or embedded content without an accessible name or alt attribute.

rules.guardNotes: Associates by aria-label, aria-labelledby or a matching label for; it does not verify visual placement.
rules.summary: Form control without an associated label.

rules.guardNotes: Flags every innerHTML/outerHTML assignment without tracing taint; it reports a sink, never an exploit.
rules.summary: Assignment to a DOM HTML sink that can execute injected markup.

rules.guardNotes: Reads integrity and crossorigin attributes only; never fetches the asset and never validates the hash.
rules.summary: Remote script or stylesheet without a Subresource Integrity attribute.

rules.guardNotes: Attribute-presence check on the anchor itself; rel=noopener or rel=noreferrer satisfies it.
rules.summary: target="_blank" link opened without rel=noopener or rel=noreferrer.

rules.guardNotes: Flags eval and the Function constructor outright; it reports a capability, never a proven execution path.
rules.summary: Dynamic code execution through eval or the Function constructor.

rules.guardNotes: Composition over word lists: a finding requires a listed dehumanising frame predicated of a listed group of people, so the frame word alone never matches. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS002 and UE-HS003, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy, block quotations, comments and URLs never reach the rule because extraction masks those spans before any rule runs. The rule reports the matched wording as an error with deterministic confidence and passes no replacement or proposed wording for --fix. A finding flags wording for human review and never asserts that any sentence meets the legal threshold of incitement.
rules.summary: A listed group of people predicated of a listed dehumanising, pest, disease or animal frame in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Universal-quantifier and inherent-trait forms only: an accusation noun without a quantifier does not match, while a trait predicate of the group matches with or without an inherent marker. A negated universal such as "Not all foreigners are criminals" is excluded as a hedged or corrected statement. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS001 and UE-HS003, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy never reaches the rule. This rule is a heuristic: every finding says it is routed to review and never claims proof of intent, because the pattern shows collective framing rather than the state of mind of the speaker. Severity is error and no replacement or proposed wording is passed.
rules.summary: Collective blame or an inherent trait attributed to a whole listed group of people in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Base-form verbs and modal outcome constructions only: a past-tense narrative such as "Attackers killed the refugees in the camp" is not a call and never matches. The rule matches group-level demands, never individual legal process, so due-process wording about named or counted individuals stays silent. The group vocabulary is shared with UE-HS001 and UE-HS002, so swapping which group is named cannot change whether a mirrored sentence fires. Claims attributed to a reporting party are exempt through the UE-DP001 guard, and quoted copy never reaches the rule. The rule is deterministic, severity is error, and it is report-only: no finding carries replacement or proposed wording.
rules.summary: A call for exclusion or violence against a listed group of people rather than individual legal process in user-visible copy.

rules.guardNotes: Appellation shapes only — an article-led singular ("a clown") or a bare plural ("idiots") — matched on extracted copy, so quoted copy and block quotations are outside the span while a paraphrase in the writer's own voice still matches. The rule cannot judge the target or context: criticism of a policy may use the same wording, so every finding is routed to review as a warning, never declared a defect.
rules.summary: Direct insult, name-calling or contempt appellation aimed at a person or group.

rules.guardNotes: Fixed-phrase matching cannot separate a threat from idiom: the sports sentence "the squad will regret the missed penalty" matches and is routed to review, while the finance and sports collocations "crush expectations" and "crush records" are deliberately excluded by pattern — both sides are locked by fixtures. The rule never proves a threat; confidence is heuristic.
rules.summary: Threat or intimidation posture written as a fixed phrase in prose.

rules.guardNotes: The pattern proves only that an all-caps token of five or more letters stands alone: no adjacent word character, digit, hyphen or slash, and no file-name extension after it, so short initialisms fall outside it by length alone. The exemption list is finite (UNHCR, ECOSOC, SARIF, README, USAGE …) and an initialism, heading or reference word missing from it is reported, because the rule cannot tell a heading from shouting.
rules.summary: All-caps word of five letters or more in running prose.

rules.guardNotes: Case-insensitive match on two identical words separated by exactly one space in the source; the legitimate doubles had had, that that and very very are exempt (fixture gr-doubles-ok.txt). Anything else between the words — a line break, extra spaces or punctuation — never matches, so intentional repetition outside the exemption list (for example long long ago) is still reported and may need ue:ignore.
rules.summary: Unintentionally doubled word, for example the the.

rules.guardNotes: Covers exactly one space between a word and one of , . ; : ? !; only the space is reported — the presence of an exclamation mark belongs to UE-RE005. Multiple spaces before the mark, a mark that starts a hard-wrapped line and an ellipsis after the space are not matched; URLs, quotations and code are outside the copy span.
rules.summary: A space between a word and its following punctuation.

rules.guardNotes: Excludes a period preceded by another period or the ellipsis character, a period preceded by a digit (decimals such as 1.5, version numbers such as v1.2, outline numbering), single-letter initials and dotted initial chains (U.S.A., U.K., e.g., i.e., J.P.), and the abbreviations U.S., U.K., U.N., e.g., i.e., etc., Dr., Mr., Mrs., Prof., vs., a.m., p.m. and St. written directly against the next word; a period followed by a lower-case letter (index.js) never matches. The list is a conservative exemption: any other period abutting a capital — an abbreviation outside the list included — is reported, since a space is required after it, and a single-letter word ending a sentence before a capital (Annex A.The) is skipped with the initials.
rules.summary: A full stop running straight into the next word instead of ending the sentence.
